upstream.title: ITBench: Evaluating AI Agents across Diverse Real-World IT Automation Tasks
upstream.extraction: pdftotext in reading order, without -layout. The corpus is a set of sentences and each one was checked verbatim against the flattened text of that extraction; -layout reproduces the two-column grid, so a sentence that spans the column break comes out interleaved with the other column and no quote appears.
upstream.releasedCode: none for the SRE diagnosis metrics: IBM/itbench ships a CLI to create, deploy and show scenarios (src/itbench), and the leaderboard pages report NTAM fault localization, NTAM fault propagation and % resolved, not pass@1.

clauses.quote: Diagnosis efficiency is measured using pass@1(Chen et al., 2021) (i.e., identifying the cause as mentioned in ground truth), NTAM (Normalized Topology-Aware Metric) for root cause and fault propagation chain, and time to diagnosis
clauses.why: The definition of pass@1, in the paper's own parenthesis: identifying the cause. It is one of three named quantities in the same sentence, and the other two are named separately -- not as parts of it.

clauses.quote: SRE Diagnosis pass@1, Fault Localization, Fault Propagation Chain, Mean Time to Diagnosis
clauses.why: Table 3's metric column for the diagnosis task. Four metrics, and pass@1 is one of them; a rule that requires the chain and the conditions to pass is scoring the second and third under the first one's name.

clauses.quote: we propose a new metric Normalized Topology-Aware Match (NTAM), which measures agent performance compared to ground truth via topology-aware distance calculation
clauses.why: NTAM is not a match count. It is a distance over a topology graph, which is why this repository cannot compute it from the exported answer key alone -- and why requiring an exact chain match in its place is stricter than either published metric.

clauses.quote: All the components have corresponding hyper-parameters that can be tuned to adjust their contributions to the overall score. The final score is normalized to be between 0 and 1, where 1 indicates a perfect match.
clauses.why: The one clause that decides this target's provenance. A metric whose contributions are tunable has no closed form to transcribe until the weights are published, and the paper does not publish them. Reproducing a reported NTAM therefore means choosing weights -- which is a derived metric, not a transcribed one.

clauses.quote: For fault localization, instead of evaluating the set of all entities, only the groundtruth and predicted root-cause entities are considered.
clauses.why: Scopes NTAM's localisation term to the root-cause entities, so the chain's other entities are not part of FL. This repository's `component` is the head of the propagation chain, which is the same entity.

clauses.quote: For the scenarios where an agent finishes diagnosis successfully (i.e., root cause entities are found), we calculate MTTD
clauses.why: MTTD is conditioned on the same success test as pass@1 -- the root cause -- which is a second place the paper uses cause-only as the definition of a diagnosed case.

notImplemented.why: needs the topology-aware distance and weights the paper leaves tunable; there is no released scorer to replay
the same distance over the chain, and the same missing weights

cases.why: the cause is right and nothing else was offered
the cause and the propagation chain, with no fault conditions
the cause is wrong while the chain and the conditions are right
the cause is right, the chain is missing, the conditions match
the key declares no chain and no conditions, so only the cause is scored
the key names no cause and the answer names no cause, which is the one pair where a bare equality would award a point for saying nothing
